name: Caraway (Carum carvi), in oil capsule combinations and a six-herb preparation
short: Infants: salmonella outbreak, fennel-aniseed-caraway tea (not capsules). Allergy: 2 cases. Peppermint-caraway capsules: adverse events not significantly above placebo; caraway-menthol: none serious.
text: This entry covers caraway taken by mouth in three products: enteric-coated capsules of peppermint oil with caraway oil, duodenal-release capsules of caraway oil with L-menthol, and a six-herb liquid preparation (bitter candytuft, chamomile, peppermint, caraway, licorice and lemon balm). The data below belong to these combinations, not to caraway alone; no safety data were found for caraway oil on its own, and peppermint oil has its own entry. Peppermint oil with caraway oil: a 2023 Cochrane review found there may be little to no difference in adverse events from placebo (risk ratio 1.56, 95% CI 0.69 to 3.53; 3 studies, 305 participants; low certainty), and a 2019 meta-analysis of 5 trials (578 participants) found no significant difference in the total number of adverse events. Within single trials: 7 adverse events in a 45-patient placebo-controlled trial (4 with the capsules, 3 with placebo), with a causal link to treatment in one case in each group; 6 patients reporting adverse events in a 96-patient trial (5 on the capsules, 1 on placebo), described as unrelated to the trial or a worsening of the dyspepsia; and adverse events in 12 people on the capsules and 14 on cisapride in a 120-patient trial. In a 223-patient trial comparing two formulations of the combination, belching with a peppermint taste was less frequent with the enteric-coated capsule than with an enteric-soluble formulation; the abstract gives no other adverse-event figures. Caraway oil with L-menthol: in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial in 95 adults with functional dyspepsia, treatment-emergent adverse events were mild to moderate and no serious adverse events were reported; in voluntary safety surveillance after the trial, few adverse events were reported (0.0187%; the abstract does not say of what) and no serious ones were identified; voluntary reporting cannot show how often events occur. Six-herb preparation: a meta-analysis that identified four randomized trials (613 patients) found that treatment-related or severe adverse events did not differ from placebo; the abstract does not say how many of the trials the safety analysis used. Caraway extract: in a 12-week randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled study in 70 overweight and obese healthy women, a caraway water extract (a different form from the oil) caused no significant changes in blood pressure, heart rate, urine or serum blood tests compared with placebo, but red blood cell levels rose and platelet distribution width fell; no negative changes in general health were observed. Allergy: in an allergy data bank of 589 cases of food allergy, 2 food allergies to caraway were among 10 linked to the mugwort-celery-spice syndrome, and sensitisation to Apiaceae spices including caraway was frequent on skin-prick testing; in a person with occupational aniseed allergy, serum antibodies cross-reacted with caraway, coriander, fennel and dill. Children: in the allergy data bank, skin-prick sensitisation to Apiaceae spices including caraway was found in 32% of tests in children and 23% in adults, but the authors say only adults were allergic to spices. Infants: in a laboratory typing study of a 2002 to 2003 rise in Salmonella Agona infections in Germany, bacteria from infants with gastroenteritis matched those from a fennel, aniseed and caraway infusion in tea bags and from an untreated batch of aniseed imported from Turkey; the abstract reports no sample of caraway on its own, and a report of a nationwide outbreak among infants in Germany from October 2002 to July 2003 attributes it to aniseed-containing herbal tea. The title of the typing study says the outbreak was caused by the aniseed-fennel-caraway infusion; the harm reported was Salmonella infection. The cited sources give no data on pregnancy. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
